headline: Sensex drops over 500 points as private banks decline while PSU bank stocks surge following Q2 results

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Private banks and financial stocks faced selling pressure following Q2 earnings results.
High crude oil prices created concerns across broader benchmark indices.
Nifty IT index dropped by 1% adding pressure on the main indices.
Weak Asian market cues dampened investor sentiment in early trading.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped over 500 points with Nifty testing levels below 23,000.
PSU bank stocks surged up to 8%, driven by strong Q2 earnings performance.
Private bank stocks including HDFC Bank and Axis Bank fell by up to 5%.
Buying in SBI and Reliance Industries helped the market trim some early losses.
summary:
Indian stock markets traded lower today as the Sensex dropped over 500 points due to weakness in private banks and IT stocks.
PSU banks outperformed significantly, jumping up to 8% led by PNB's strong Q2 results, while private lenders like HDFC Bank and Axis Bank struggled.
Buying in heavyweights such as Reliance Industries and SBI helped indices recover from their sharp early morning losses.
